text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer notes the base E 350 is rated 25/33/28 mpg (city/highway/combined) versus 28/35/31 mpg for the 530i. Reviewer judges both sedans refined and poised and calls the choice of driving feel a matter of taste. Reviewer favours the E-Class for buyers who want the newest tech, citing the Superscreen, Burmester 4D audio and an optional AI that learns routines. KBB's spec comparison shows the E-Class with less rear headroom (37.6 vs 39.1 in) and rear legroom (36.2 vs 37.0 in) than the 5 Series. Reviewer notes every E-Class variant gains a center airbag. Reviewer lists a KBB Fair Purchase Price of $58,000 for the E 350 versus $54,700 for the 530i, while calling overall pricing similar. Reviewer notes the E-Class powertrain warranty (4 years/50,000 miles) is shorter than the 5 Series' 6 years/70,000 miles.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer praises a smooth, calm ride with a quiet electric powertrain. Reviewer states the low center of gravity gives agility and optional rear-wheel steering adds highway stability and a tight turning circle. Reviewer calls the EQE 350 4MATIC's roughly 6-second 0-60 mph time not brilliant and notes the i5 eDrive40 is 0.3 s quicker. Reviewer notes the EQE 350+ is rated at 308 miles of range versus 295 miles for the base i5 eDrive40. Reviewer lists as a con that the EQE 350 4MATIC and 500 4MATIC dropped to 267 miles of range, from 298. Reviewer states 10-80 % DC fast charging takes about 30 minutes, similar to the BMW i5. Reviewer describes the cabin as high-tech and luxurious, with comfortable seats and high-quality materials. Reviewer states the EQE's rear seat is roomier than the E-Class's, with no transmission tunnel. Reviewer notes the swooping roofline means bending more to get into the car. Reviewer calls the 11-cu-ft trunk small; the i5 offers 17.3 cu ft. Reviewer praises the full-width Hyperscreen and calls the EQE's tech superb. Reviewer notes KBB Fair Purchase Prices run about $4,850-5,550 below MSRP and expects above-average resale values.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer states the 365-hp dual-motor Electrified G80 launches quickly in Sport mode. Reviewer states the estimated 282-mile range never caused range anxiety during the test. Reviewer lists the range below 300 miles as a con. Reviewer states the car is no sports sedan but handles mountain roads willingly, with great grip and above-average steering feel, and is quiet and smooth in Normal mode. Reviewer notes steering-wheel paddles adjust regenerative braking up to one-pedal driving. Reviewer warns that the round infotainment dial and the similar round gear-selector dial are easy to confuse. Reviewer states the heated and cooled front seats stay comfortable all day and include a leg and back massage function. Reviewer states rear legroom is snugger than in the gas G80. Reviewer states the trunk (10.8 cu ft) is slightly smaller than the gas G80's. Reviewer describes the cabin as posh and tech-heavy, with forged-wood trim and eco-friendly fabrics. Reviewer lists the many standard safety and assistance systems as a pro, including Highway Driving Assist, surround view and remote smart parking. Reviewer lists the single available trim as a con. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «never gave us anxiety»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer praises the smooth, comfort-oriented ride and would skip the F Sport Handling option with adaptive suspension. Reviewer lists the roomy cabin as a pro, with 39.2 in of rear legroom and angled rear seatbacks for headroom. Reviewer notes the rear seats do not split or fold. Reviewer calls the ES 300h's 215 hp not especially impressive. Reviewer highlights the ES 300h hybrid's 44 mpg combined rating. Reviewer calls the fuel economy of the gasoline-only ES 250 and ES 350 more tolerable than remarkable. Reviewer describes the cabin as calm and spacious with quality materials. Reviewer calls the ES relatively affordable for a luxury sedan, with strong resale value. Reviewer lists as a con that all-wheel drive is only available with the base engine. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «not especially impressive» «more tolerable than remarkable»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer lists tame performance as a con; even the quickest dual-motor ES 500e is tame compared with rivals. Reviewer finds the ES 350h hybrid noisy under hard acceleration, while the EVs are free of that engine noise. Reviewer notes the 244-hp ES 350h prioritizes efficiency, with Lexus estimating up to 46 mpg combined. Reviewer finds some interior materials odd, singling out the synthetic suede on the steering wheel, and suggests traditionalists may prefer real leather. Reviewer finds the front seats roomy even for tall drivers and the rear adult-friendly, with 40.7 in of rear legroom (1.5 in more than the outgoing ES). Reviewer praises the new infotainment system's crisper resolution and home button. Reviewer finds the tactile HVAC control bar below the screen easy to use. Reviewer finds the physical roller volume dial easy to use. Reviewer states the hybrid rides pleasantly. Reviewer calls the hybrid a uniquely good value with class-leading resale, noting the EV ES starts below $50,000 while the BMW i5 and Mercedes EQE start in the high $60,000s.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer cites 0-60 mph in 3.1 s for the standard AWD and a claimed 1.99 s for the 1,020-hp Plaid. Reviewer finds the standard adaptive suspension controlled and comfortable for daily driving, though not as smooth as a Mercedes-Benz EQE. Reviewer finds the handling lively when pushed, though less sporty than a Porsche Taycan. Reviewer finds the standard yoke a bit awkward and notes a round wheel is available at no extra cost. Reviewer praises the 17-inch screen's crisp graphics and fast responses and notes Netflix and Hulu streaming is supported. Reviewer notes Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are not supported. Reviewer highlights EPA ranges of 402 miles (AWD) and 348 miles (Plaid) and combined efficiency of 124 MPGe. Reviewer praises the Supercharger network, noting charging to about 80% in as little as 30 minutes at a 250-kW charger. Reviewer finds the cabin sparse and says it should be plusher, with better fit and finish for the price. Reviewer notes rear legroom of 35.5 inches is only slightly more than the Model 3, though the car is wide. Reviewer praises 25 cu ft of cargo space (61.4 cu ft with the seats folded), the 3.1 cu ft frunk and the wide opening. Reviewer notes the fair purchase price is above MSRP and the 5-year cost to own is among the highest for high-end luxury cars, though resale values are above average. Reviewer calls the reliability record patchy, citing panel gaps, paint flaws, loose weather strips and long service waits.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer (dual-motor Prestige) finds the power delivery linear and predictable. Reviewer finds the ride on the adaptive air suspension composed and supple on all surfaces. Reviewer finds the steering perfectly responsive and the car a pleasure to drive. Reviewer welcomes the addition of one-pedal driving, which earlier Audi EVs lacked but most rivals offer. Reviewer states the car (up to 392 mi single-motor, 377 mi dual-motor) beats its BMW and Mercedes rivals on range quite easily and comes close to the Model S's 402 miles. Reviewer highlights the 800-volt system, which charges from 10% to 80% in 21 minutes on a DC fast charger. Reviewer finds the optional front-passenger screen useful for changing navigation, and it cannot be seen from the driver's seat. Reviewer notes the infotainment responds to more than 800 spoken commands. Reviewer describes the interior as a pleasant mix of class and simplicity, with attention to textures. Reviewer finds the 35.2 in of rear legroom acceptable; an average-size adult fits behind a driver of the same size. Reviewer notes 26 cu ft of cargo space behind the rear seats versus 17.3 cu ft in the BMW i5, and 39.9 cu ft with the seats folded. Reviewer finds the cabin quiet, with dual-pane front side windows on the top trim limiting wind noise. Reviewer calls the optional Bang & Olufsen surround system, with headrest speakers, excellent. Reviewer likes the large optional sunroof, which lets in light without heat and switches from clear to opaque at the touch of a button. Reviewer calls the $67,195 starting price competitive and says the car may be a new class leader.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer notes the A6's 23 mpg combined rating trails the BMW 540i xDrive's 28 mpg. Reviewer notes the BMW 5 Series and Mercedes E-Class have slightly larger trunks than the A6. Reviewer thinks the new A6 looks great inside, though Audi has caught up with interior design trends rather than led them.
